sections.html:
Craighead County is in northeast Arkansas, with Crowley's Ridge running through it, and it has two county seats: Jonesboro in the western district and Lake City in the eastern district. Jonesboro is the largest city. Other incorporated places include Bono, Black Oak, Caraway, Brookland, Monette, Bay, Egypt, Cash and Nettleton, which sits partly inside Jonesboro. The 2020 population was 111,231, and Arkansas State University is a major presence in the county.

A tax bill here depends on which city, school district and improvement district the parcel falls in, and not only on the county. Two houses with the same value can carry different bills.

sections.h2: Who sends the bill and who sets the value
sections.html:
Two offices do separate jobs. The Assessor sets the value, and the Tax Collector bills and collects the money.

OfficeAddressPhone
Assessor511 S. Union St., Suite 130, Jonesboro870-933-4572
Tax Collector511 Union Street, Suite 107, Jonesboro; second office at 107 Cobean, Lake City870-933-4560

Collections are turned over to the County Treasurer at the end of each month for distribution. Most of the money goes to schools, and the rest is split among county offices, cities, fire and police pensions, libraries, roads, streets and improvement districts, depending on where the property sits. The Assessor appraises property and takes personal property reports. The Circuit Clerk records deeds and mortgages.

Taxable value is 20 percent of the Assessor's appraised value, and that figure is multiplied by the millage rate for the location. One mill equals one tenth of a cent. Voters in the area approve the rate.

Real estate is assessed to the owner of record as of January 1, and taxes run one year behind: each year's assessment is billed the following year. If you sell during the year, the bill for the prior assessment year is still outstanding until paid, and it is usually settled through the title company at closing.

Arkansas appraisers revisit properties every 3, 4 or 5 years, looking at the size, quality and condition of improvements along with sales and rental data. If you add a room, build a garage or turn an owner-occupied house into a rental, tell the Assessor.

The Tax Collector accepts payments from the first business day of March through October 15 of the year after the assessment. After that date the taxes are delinquent, a 10 percent penalty is added under Arkansas Code 26-35-501, and delinquent real estate taxes accrue interest daily. A payment sent by mail counts as timely if it is postmarked by October 15, and the collector suggests buying postage at the counter or asking for a hand postmark.

  • Online payment is offered through the county's payment portal.
  • For delinquent personal property, the office takes cash, money order, cashier's check or card (fees apply) and no personal checks.
  • The collector must publish delinquent lists each year. The personal property list goes to a local newspaper before December 1.

Personal property is separate from real estate, but unpaid personal property can complicate a payment day. Ask the office what is attached to your name before you plan a closing.

Start with the Assessor, because wrong square footage or a wrong property description can often be corrected without a hearing. If the dispute is about value, the last day to schedule a hearing with the County Board of Equalization is the third Monday in August. The board hears the owner's side and decides whether to adjust the value. Ask the Assessor's office for the current equalization schedule and forms.

Homeowners may qualify for a homestead credit under Amendment 79 for a principal residence, and owners 65 or older or totally disabled may qualify for a freeze on taxable value. The credit was $600 at last report, and the legislature has considered raising it, so check with the Assessor before counting on a number.

Unpaid taxes can lead to a tax-delinquent land sale run through the Arkansas Commissioner of State Lands. These sales are held as regional auctions that cover Craighead and neighboring counties. Bidding starts at the taxes, penalties and interest owed. Owners can redeem until 4 p.m. on the last business day before the sale, and under Act 241, effective July 1, 2023, a sale at auction is final. Parcels that do not sell appear on an online list about 30 days later.

Selling first can stop the clock. A buyer who closes through a title company gets the bill paid from the proceeds, and nothing is left to certify.

A sale is recorded with the Circuit Clerk, who acts as county recorder. The fee schedule is $15 for the first page of a deed, $5 for each additional page and a $300 cap on multi-instrument documents. Arkansas also charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on deals above $100. Who pays it is settled in the contract.

  • Get a payoff or tax statement from the Tax Collector.
  • Check whether any personal property tax sits under the same owner name.
  • Confirm the deed's legal description against the Assessor's parcel record.
  • Ask the title company to pay the tax and record the deed the same day.

If the house has tenants, gather the lease and rent records before you list, since a buyer and the title company will ask for them.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Craighead County?
faqs.a: The Craighead County Tax Collector, at 511 Union Street, Suite 107 in Jonesboro and 107 Cobean in Lake City. The phone number is 870-933-4560.

faqs.q: What is the property tax deadline in Craighead County?
faqs.a: October 15 each year. Later payments carry a 10 percent penalty plus daily interest on real estate.

faqs.q: How do I challenge my Craighead County assessment?
faqs.a: Contact the County Assessor first, then request a hearing before the County Board of Equalization. The last day to schedule one is the third Monday in August.

faqs.q: Does a mailed payment count if it is postmarked by October 15?
faqs.a: Yes. The collector cites Arkansas Code 26-35-501(c)(3)(A) and recommends getting a manual postmark at the counter to avoid delays.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Craighead County house that owes back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax is paid from sale proceeds at closing. A tax-delinquent parcel can also be sold at a state auction, which is final, so settle the balance before the sale date if you want to keep the property.
